name: Indian Rat Snake
habitat: Almost anywhere: farmland, gardens, villages, scrub, forests and mangroves; often around roofs, wood piles, tree hollows and rat holes
range: Throughout India and the rest of the subcontinent, and into South-East Asia
diet: Rats, frogs, lizards, birds and their eggs, and other snakes
ids: Very long, slim and fast-moving, usually 2 m or more, with a long tail that makes up about a quarter of its length.
Narrow head, barely wider than the neck, with large, round, dark eyes.
Brownish to olive-yellow body. The scales on the rear half are edged in black, giving a net-like or cross-barred look, while the front half is plainer. Lips and chin are creamy.
Cannot spread a true hood, though it may flatten its neck, hiss and rear up like a cobra.
Smooth scales and round pupils; the belly is pale yellow or cream.

look.colour: Olive-brown to yellowish; cream lips and belly
look.pattern: Dark scale edges on the rear body give a net-like or barred look
look.head: Long, narrow head with large round eyes
look.body: Long, slender and smooth, with a long tail

fact: The Dhaman is often mistaken for a cobra and killed, though it is completely harmless and one of the best natural controllers of rats.

name: Common Wolf Snake
habitat: Houses, gardens, farmland, forests and rocky areas; often enters buildings at night
range: Throughout most of India, plus Sri Lanka, Nepal, Pakistan, Bangladesh and South-East Asia
diet: Geckos and other small lizards, skinks, small frogs, mice and small snakes
ids: Slim, shiny brown to chocolate body with fine, narrow whitish cross-bars, most distinct on the front half and fading or breaking up towards the tail. Older snakes can look nearly plain.
Flat head clearly wider than the slim neck, often with pale mottling, and large eyes with vertical pupils.
Smooth scales all along the back, with no enlarged row of scales on the spine (the key difference from a krait).
Pale belly. Fast and nervous; it bites readily if picked up but is harmless.

look.pattern: Thin pale cross-bars, clearer on the front half
look.head: Flat head wider than the neck, vertical pupils

fact: This harmless gecko-hunter is the snake most often killed in mistake for a krait. A krait has a row of enlarged six-sided scales down its back, which a wolf snake lacks.

name: Green Vine Snake
habitat: Shrubs, hedges, gardens, scrub and forest; lives in bushes and low trees
range: Most of peninsular India, the Western and Eastern Ghats and the north-east (several very similar species share this green vine-snake look, so they are grouped here)
diet: Garden lizards and other lizards, frogs and sometimes small birds
ids: Extremely slender, long, bright leaf-green body (sometimes yellowish or grey-brown) that looks just like a vine.
Long, pointed head with a snout that ends in a sharp tip.
Horizontal, keyhole-shaped pupils, which are unique among Indian snakes.
A pale yellow or white line along the lower flank on each side; black and white skin between the scales shows when it puffs up its neck.
Sways slowly like a twig in the wind and may gape to show a dark mouth lining.

look.pattern: Plain, with a pale line along each side
look.head: Long pointed head with keyhole-shaped pupils
look.body: Very long and thin, smooth scales

fact: The horizontal pupils give vine snakes forward-facing vision so they can judge the distance to a lizard before they strike. Their mild venom is harmless to people.

name: Indo-Chinese Rat Snake
habitat: Forest edges, bamboo, tea gardens, paddy fields and scrub in humid hills and plains
range: North-east India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura, Mizoram, Nagaland) and eastwards into South-East Asia
diet: Frogs, lizards, small mammals and birds
ids: A long, slender, fast-moving brown or olive snake with a long thin tail.
Large, dark eyes and a narrow head; the scale edges are dark, giving a lightly netted pattern on the hind body.
Smooth scales; the lips and chin are yellowish or cream, and the belly is pale.
The north-eastern cousin of the Indian Rat Snake, but slimmer and usually more olive or brownish-yellow.

look.pattern: Dark scale edges create a faint net on the hind body
look.head: Narrow head with large round eyes
look.body: Long, slim and smooth with a long tail

name: Green Rat Snake
habitat: Hill forest, bamboo and scrub near streams, often on the ground or low in vegetation
range: Himalayan foothills and hills of north-east India (Sikkim, West Bengal hills, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland)
diet: Frogs, lizards, small mammals and birds
ids: Bright to dark green body with a yellow-green or yellowish head and a black line along the edge of each belly scale.
Very long, slender and fast, with a long tail; smooth scales and large round eyes.
Often shows a pale stripe on each side of the body and a black-edged line at the lower flank.
Harmless, though green like a vine snake or green pit viper; large round pupils separate it from both.

look.pattern: Faint dark and pale lines along the flanks
look.head: Long narrow head with large round eyes

name: Common Trinket Snake
habitat: Gardens, farmland, villages, scrub and forest; hides under rocks, in walls and in rat holes
range: Most of peninsular India, the Western Ghats and the north-east; also Sri Lanka, Nepal and Pakistan
diet: Rats, mice, lizards and small birds
active: Mostly by day and at dusk
ids: A slim, fast brown snake with a pattern of dark, rounded saddles or cross-bars, together with two dark lines along the back that merge into a dark stripe on the rear body.
Dark stripes run from the eye to the lip and across the eye, as if the snake wore a mask. Head is long and pointed.
Colour varies from grey-brown to reddish-brown and olive; the belly is cream.
Smooth scales and a long tail; when threatened it flattens its body and may shake its tail like a vibrating rattle.

look.pattern: Dark saddles that fade into two stripes towards the tail
look.head: Long head with dark eye stripes
look.body: Slim and smooth with a long tail

fact: When cornered the Common Trinket Snake vibrates its tail against the ground, making a buzzing sound like a tiny rattlesnake.

name: Copper-headed Trinket Snake
habitat: Forest edges, fields, villages and bamboo; often near water and in rat burrows
range: North-east India, the Himalayan foothills and the eastern plains; also Bangladesh and South-East Asia
ids: A coppery or reddish-brown head and forebody, with dark stripes radiating from the eye like spokes (hence its other name, the Radiated Rat Snake).
Several dark stripes along the body that fade towards the tail; the body is brown, yellowish or greyish.
Big, round pupils and a long, slim body, sometimes with a dark spot behind the neck.
Flattens its neck, rears up and strikes if cornered, often mistaken for a cobra, but it is not venomous.

look.colour: Coppery-brown head, brown or grey body
look.pattern: Dark stripes along the body; radiating stripes by the eye
look.head: Reddish head with dark radiating marks

name: Himalayan Trinket Snake
habitat: Mountain forest, scrub and stone walls in the Himalaya at 1,000 to 3,000 m
range: Western and central Himalaya: Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, also Nepal
ids: Olive-brown to yellowish-green snake with a network of dark scale edges and a pale, yellowish throat.
Slender, strong body with weakly keeled scales and a rounded, slightly flat head.
Found in the cool mountains of the western Himalaya; it is non-venomous.

look.pattern: Dark scale edges give a netted look
look.head: Rounded head with a yellowish throat

name: Cantor's Trinket Snake
habitat: Hill forest, tea gardens, farmland and roadsides in damp mountains
range: Eastern Himalaya and north-eastern hills (Sikkim, West Bengal hills, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland)
ids: Olive to brown body with dark blotches or crossbars and a reddish or pinkish tint along the flanks and the skin between the scales.
Slender head, large round eyes and smooth scales; pale yellowish belly.
A harmless snake of the eastern Himalayan hills.

look.colour: Olive to brown with reddish skin between the scales
look.pattern: Dark blotches or crossbars
look.head: Slender head with large eyes

name: Black-banded Trinket Snake
habitat: Hill forest, bamboo, tea gardens and farmland, on the ground and in leaf litter
range: North-east India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, West Bengal hills) and eastwards
ids: Slender snake in orange-red, reddish-brown or yellow-brown with a series of broad black bands (in some local forms only a thin dark stripe along the back).
Small, narrow head with a black marking behind the eye; shiny, smooth scales.
Several colour forms exist, from banded and bright to plain red; the belly is cream.

look.pattern: Black bands (some are plain red with a thin line)
look.head: Small narrow head with a dark band behind the eye

name: Glossy-bellied Racer
habitat: Dry open country: desert edge, scrub, rocky hills, fields and villages
range: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and dry parts of the peninsula; also Pakistan and the Middle East
diet: Lizards, geckos, small rodents and insects
ids: A slim, alert, very fast snake in sandy, grey or olive-brown colours with dark spots or cross-bars along the body.
Large eyes, round pupils and a slender head, barely wider than the neck; smooth, shiny scales.
Moves quickly over open ground and rocky terrain, often with the head raised.

look.pattern: Dark spots or cross-bars, often fading with age
look.head: Slender head with large round eyes

name: Platyceps plinii
habitat: Rocky plateaus, scrub, farmland and villages in the dry parts of the peninsula
range: Western and central India, especially Maharashtra and Gujarat
ids: A slim, plain tan, brown or reddish-brown racer, sometimes with faint dark spotting on the front of the body.
Large round eyes, a narrow head and smooth scales; a pale belly.
Fast and nervous; escapes over rocks and into crevices.

look.pattern: Plain, sometimes faint spots or bars near the head
look.head: Slender head with large eyes

name: Slender Racer
habitat: Rocky hills, scrub and dry grassland
range: Dry parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka and Rajasthan
ids: A very slender small racer in pale brown or grey with dark cross-bars or blotches, which are bold on the front of the body.
Large eyes, a narrow head and smooth scales.
Lives among rocks and in dry scrub.

look.pattern: Dark cross-bars and blotches
look.head: Narrow head with large eyes

name: Platyceps bholanathi
habitat: Rocky, dry scrub country and boulder-strewn hills
range: Deccan plateau (Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu)
ids: A small, slender, sandy-brown racer with darker cross-bars or blotches along the front of the body.
Large eyes and a narrow head; very fast, retreating into rock crevices.

look.pattern: Dark cross-bars and blotches
look.head: Narrow head with large eyes

name: Royal Snake
habitat: Deserts, semi-desert, dry scrub, farmland and villages
range: Rajasthan, Gujarat and the north-western dry zone; also Pakistan
ids: A handsome, heavy-bodied snake with large brown or reddish blotches (often joined into a zigzag) on a pale tan or yellowish body.
Black or dark head and neck in some, and a pale belly; smooth scales.
Hisses loudly and flattens its neck; harmless, though it often gets mistaken for a viper or cobra.

look.colour: Tan or yellowish with brown or red blotches
look.pattern: Large blotches joined into a zigzag
look.head: Rounded head, dark in some

name: Travancore Wolf Snake
habitat: Evergreen and moist forest, plantations, gardens and houses in the hills
range: Western Ghats (Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu)
ids: Dark brown to blue-black snake whose paired or speckled white-yellow bands form a chain-like pattern, clearest on young snakes and fading on old ones.
Flat, broad head, wider than the neck, with large eyes and vertical pupils.
Smooth scales along the whole back (no enlarged row down the spine) and a flat head wider than the neck.
A krait look-alike of the Western Ghats that is completely harmless.

look.colour: Dark brown to blue-black with yellow-white markings
look.pattern: Narrow white-yellow chain-like bands, fading with age
look.head: Flat head wider than the neck, vertical pupils

name: Banded Wolf Snake
habitat: Dry and moist forest, scrub, rocky ground, farmland and houses
range: Peninsular India: the Western Ghats, Deccan and Eastern Ghats
ids: Brown or grey-brown with narrow, paler, dark-edged cross-bands along the body (white-ringed on the young) and a dark head.
Flat head wider than the neck, large eyes and vertical pupils.
Smooth scales along the whole back (no enlarged row down the spine) and a flat head wider than the neck.

look.pattern: Narrow pale cross-bands, white in the young
look.head: Flat head wider than the neck

name: Barred Wolf Snake
habitat: Rocky scrub, forest, farmland and the walls and floors of houses
range: Peninsular India and the Western and Eastern Ghats
ids: Glossy black or dark brown with sharp white or cream cross-bars, which are broad and clear on the neck and front of the body and may fade along the tail.
Flat head, wider than the neck, with big eyes and vertical pupils.
Smooth scales along the whole back (no enlarged row down the spine) and a flat head wider than the neck.
One of the commonest snakes mistaken for a krait. It is harmless and bites only if handled.

look.colour: Glossy black or dark brown; white belly
look.pattern: Crisp white or cream bars, clearer on the front
look.head: Flat head, wide neck-notch, vertical pupils

name: Yellow-speckled Wolf Snake
habitat: Forest, stone walls, tea gardens and farmland in the hills
range: Himalayan foothills and north-east India (Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh)
ids: Olive-brown to yellowish-brown snake with a fine pattern of pale yellow speckles that form a faint net or narrow bands.
Shiny, smooth scales and a flat, rounded head with vertical pupils.
Less boldly marked than other wolf snakes; found only in the Himalayan and north-eastern hills.

look.pattern: Fine pale speckles, sometimes faint bands
look.head: Flat head with vertical pupils

name: Bridal Snake
habitat: Forest edges, scrub, plantations and houses in the peninsula
range: Peninsular India, the Western Ghats and Tamil Nadu
ids: Slender snake in dark chocolate brown with narrow, paired white or yellowish cross-bands that run all the way round the body.
Flat head with a pale blotch or collar and vertical pupils.
Smooth scales along the whole back (no enlarged row down the spine) and a flat head wider than the neck.

look.colour: Chocolate brown with white or yellow bands
look.pattern: Narrow paired cross-bands
look.head: Flat head with vertical pupils

name: Yellow-collared Wolf Snake
habitat: Rocky dry forest, scrub and farmland, often among boulders and walls
range: Western Ghats foothills and the dry peninsula, mostly Karnataka and Telangana
ids: Glossy dark chocolate-brown or purplish body with a clear yellow or cream collar across the back of the head and neck.
Flat head and large eyes with vertical pupils; plain body in adults, which may be lightly banded when young.
Smooth scales along the whole back (no enlarged row down the spine) and a flat head wider than the neck.

look.pattern: Plain body, yellow neck band
look.head: Flat head with a yellow collar

name: White-banded Wolf Snake
habitat: Forest edges, scrub, farmland and houses in the hills
range: Eastern Himalaya and north-east India (Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Assam, West Bengal hills)
ids: Glossy blackish-brown snake with broad, clean white or cream bands that look boldly like a banded krait or sea krait.
Flat, rounded head with vertical pupils; a pale chin and belly.
Smooth scales along the whole back (no enlarged row down the spine) and a flat head wider than the neck.

look.pattern: Broad white or cream bands
look.head: Flat head with vertical pupils

name: Zaw's Wolf Snake
habitat: Hill forest, plantations and roadsides
range: North-east India (Mizoram, Assam, West Bengal hills, Arunachal Pradesh) and eastwards
ids: Dark brown to black wolf snake with narrow white spots or incomplete cross-bars, often brighter on the young.
Flat head with vertical pupils and smooth scales; a pale belly.

look.pattern: Narrow white spots or bars
look.head: Flat head with vertical pupils

name: Andaman Wolf Snake
habitat: Forest, plantations, gardens and houses on the islands
range: Andaman and Nicobar Islands (endemic)
ids: Dark brown to grey-brown snake, often with pale spots or faint cross-bands and a lighter belly.
Flat head, large eyes with vertical pupils; smooth scales.
The commonest wolf-type snake on the Andaman Islands.

look.pattern: Faint pale spots or narrow bands
look.head: Flat head with vertical pupils

name: Common Mock Viper
habitat: Hill forest floor, scrub, bamboo and plantations, among leaf litter, rocks and low vegetation
range: North-east India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram) and eastwards
ids: A small, brown to reddish-brown or yellowish snake with fine darker flecks, a few pale stripes and a dark streak through the eye.
A broad, flat head, widened at the jaws, and vertical pupils, so it looks like a small viper, but it has smooth scales and a slim body.
When disturbed it flattens its head, raises its neck and strikes; its mild rear-fanged venom is harmless to people.

look.colour: Brown, reddish-brown or yellowish with dark flecks
look.pattern: Faint pale stripes and dark specks; dark eye streak
look.head: Broad flat head with vertical pupils

name: Duméril's Black-headed Snake
habitat: Leaf litter, stone walls, scrub and gardens in dry and moist forest
range: Peninsular India: the Western Ghats, Deccan and Eastern Ghats
ids: A slim, fast, glossy snake in brown, reddish-brown or orange-brown with a black head.
The black head carries a pale yellow or white band across the snout and a second pale band at the neck, like a collar.
Long, thin tail; smooth scales; the belly is pale and often tinged with orange.
A harmless skink-hunter that is quick to flee under stones.

look.colour: Brown, reddish or orange-brown; black head
look.pattern: Pale bands on the black head and neck
look.head: Small black head with pale bands
look.body: Very slender and smooth with a long tail

name: Many-banded Cat Snake
habitat: Forest edges, scrub, rocky slopes and farmland in the western Himalaya at 500 to 2,000 m
range: Western and central Himalaya (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh) and Nepal
diet: Lizards, birds and their eggs, and small rodents
ids: A slim grey-brown or olive-brown snake with a pattern of many dark cross-bars or a net of dark blotches.
A broad head clearly distinct from the thin neck, big golden-orange eyes and vertical pupils.
Smooth scales and a long tail; coiled on rocks or in bushes by day. Mildly venomous but harmless to people.

look.pattern: Many dark cross-bars or blotches
look.head: Broad head distinct from the neck; golden eyes with vertical pupils

name: Common Bronzeback Tree Snake
habitat: Gardens, hedges, scrub, farmland and forest; climbs quickly into bushes, trees and house walls
range: Most of India, especially peninsular India and the Western Ghats (several near-identical bronzebacks are grouped here)
diet: Geckos, lizards, frogs and tree frogs
ids: A very slender, fast tree snake with a glossy bronze, olive or coppery-brown back and a pale yellow or cream lower flank.
A black stripe runs from the snout through the large round eye and along the side of the neck, with a pale stripe above and below it.
Very large eyes with round pupils and a long, whip-like tail; smooth scales.
When alarmed it inflates its neck and shows bright blue skin between the scales. It is harmless.

look.colour: Bronze, olive or coppery brown; cream or yellow flank
look.pattern: Black eye stripe, pale side stripes
look.head: Narrow head with large round eyes
look.body: Extremely slender and smooth, with a whip-like tail

fact: When a bronzeback inflates its throat, a flash of blue skin appears between the scales. Predators think twice, and a person seeing it for the first time may too.

name: Large-eyed Bronzeback
habitat: Moist forest, plantations and forest edges, in shrubs and low trees
range: Western Ghats (Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu)
ids: Slender tree snake that is greenish, bluish-green or olive-brown above, with a pale yellow lip line and flank stripe.
Particularly large, dark, round eyes and a long, narrow head.
Looks similar to the Common Bronzeback; its bluer-green tone and larger eye are the clues.

look.pattern: Pale lip line and flank stripe
look.head: Narrow head with very large eyes

name: Andaman Bronzeback
habitat: Forest, gardens and plantations, in shrubs and trees
range: Andaman and Nicobar Islands (endemic)
ids: A slender tree snake that is bright green on the front of the body and blue-green or bronze towards the tail, with a thin yellow or white side stripe.
Large golden eyes with round pupils, and a long, whip-like tail.
The common bronzeback of the Andaman Islands; its green-blue colour is eye-catching.

look.colour: Bright green to blue-green, bronze towards the tail
look.pattern: Thin yellow side stripe
look.head: Narrow head with large golden eyes

name: Boulenger's Bronzeback
habitat: Forest edges, bamboo, tea gardens and hedges; often on low bushes and the ground
range: North-east India (Assam, Tripura, Mizoram, West Bengal and nearby hills)
ids: Slender brown or olive snake with a bold black stripe through the eye and along the neck, edged with orange-yellow and cream stripes.
The head and neck are often orange-tinged; large round eyes and a long, thin tail.
A north-eastern bronzeback, harmless and very fast.

look.colour: Brown or olive; orange-yellow on the head and neck
look.pattern: Bold black eye stripe with pale stripes
look.head: Narrow head with large round eyes

name: Gray Cat Snake
habitat: Forest edges, bamboo, plantations and villages, in trees, bushes and on the ground
range: North-east India (Assam, West Bengal hills, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh) and eastwards
diet: Lizards, small birds, rodents and frogs
ids: Slim, grey to brown snake marked with dark cross-bars, blotches or net-like patterns, and a pale throat with dark bars.
A wide head clearly separated from a thin neck, large eyes and vertical pupils.
Smooth scales and a long tail; coils on branches by day. Mildly venomous, harmless to people.

look.pattern: Dark cross-bars or blotches
look.head: Wide head distinct from the neck; vertical pupils

name: Light-barred Kukri Snake
habitat: Hill forest, tea gardens and farmland, in leaf litter, under stones and logs
range: North-east India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Mizoram)
ids: A slender kukri snake in reddish-brown, grey-brown or orange-brown with thin, pale (white or cream) cross-bars, and a dark blotch pattern or chevron on the head.
A short, blunt head barely wider than the neck and smooth scales.
Enlarged rear teeth shaped like a Gurkha kukri knife are used to slit open reptile eggs. It is harmless but bites readily if handled.

look.pattern: Thin pale cross-bars; dark head marking
look.head: Short blunt head

name: Common Cat Snake
habitat: Dry scrub, rocky country, farmland, villages and houses; climbs into bushes, trees, roofs and walls at night
range: Most of the drier parts of India (Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and the Deccan), also Pakistan and Sri Lanka
diet: Geckos and other lizards, small birds and rodents
ids: A slim, light grey, tan or sandy-brown snake with a pattern of dark (grey-brown) bars or blotches, often forming a net or ladder pattern.
A characteristic dark, arrow- or Y-shaped mark on the top of the broad head, with a dark streak behind each eye.
Broad head distinct from a thin neck, large eyes with vertical pupils and smooth scales.
Rests curled on a branch or in a wall during the day. Mildly venomous, but harmless to people.

look.colour: Pale grey, tan or sandy brown
look.pattern: Dark bars or net-like blotches; arrow mark on the head
look.head: Broad head distinct from the neck; vertical pupils
look.body: Slim and laterally flattened, smooth scales

name: Forsten's Cat Snake
habitat: Forests, scrub, farmland, villages and the roofs of houses; hides in tree hollows, rock crevices and thatched roofs
range: Most of peninsular India, central India and the Western Ghats; also Sri Lanka
diet: Rodents, birds and their eggs, lizards and bats
ids: One of the largest cat snakes: a thick-bodied, long snake that can reach 2 m or more.
Variable: grey-brown with dark zigzag or blotched crossbars (some with a bold black-and-white pattern), or plain tan, brown or yellowish.
Broad head distinct from a thin neck, large eyes with vertical pupils and smooth scales.
Large, heavily built head and a laterally flattened body. Mildly venomous, but harmless to people.

look.colour: Grey, tan or brown; some plain pale or orange
look.pattern: Dark zigzag blotches or crossbars, or plain
look.head: Large broad head; vertical pupils
look.body: Long, heavy and flattened from side to side

name: Collared Cat Snake
habitat: Moist and evergreen forest, plantations and gardens, on shrubs, trees and walls
range: Western Ghats of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu (endemic)
diet: Lizards, frogs, geckos and small birds
ids: A slender snake in light tan, brown, orange or brick-red with dark cross-bars or irregular blotches, plus a dark patch across the neck.
Broad head distinct from a thin neck, large eyes with vertical pupils and smooth scales.
Seen coiled on leaves and branches at night in Western Ghats forests.

look.pattern: Dark crossbars or blotches with a dark neck patch
look.head: Broad head distinct from the neck

name: Beddome's Cat Snake
habitat: Moist forest, plantations, farm edges and houses in the northern Western Ghats, on shrubs and trees
range: Northern Western Ghats of Maharashtra and Goa (also reported in Karnataka)
ids: A slender brown or tan cat snake with dark crossbars or chevron-like marks along the back and a pale belly.
Broad head distinct from a thin neck, large eyes with vertical pupils and smooth scales.
A common night-time visitor to gardens and houses in the Konkan region.

look.pattern: Dark crossbars or chevrons
look.head: Broad head distinct from the neck

name: Thackeray's Cat Snake
habitat: Evergreen and moist forest, plantations and gardens, on shrubs and low trees
range: Western Ghats of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu (endemic)
ids: A slender yellowish-brown to golden snake with a pattern of dark brown, irregular crossbars and flecks.
Broad head distinct from a thin neck, large eyes with vertical pupils and smooth scales.
Usually found coiled on leaves or branches at night in Western Ghats forests.

look.pattern: Dark brown irregular bars and flecks
look.head: Broad head distinct from the neck

name: Yellow-green Cat Snake
habitat: Dry and moist forest, scrub and gardens, on bushes and trees
range: Peninsular India: Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu
ids: A yellow-green, olive or greenish-brown cat snake with a network of dark spots or fine crossbars.
Broad head distinct from a thin neck, large eyes with vertical pupils and smooth scales.
Looks quite green at night, so people confuse it with vine snakes or green pit vipers, but its pupils are vertical and its body is more heavily built than a vine snake.

look.pattern: Dark spots or net-like crossbars
look.head: Broad head distinct from the neck

name: Green Cat Snake
habitat: Evergreen forest and forest edges, in trees and bushes
range: North-east India (Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Tripura, Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh)
ids: A bright green cat snake (sometimes yellow-green or orange-brown), with a blue-white or pale blue throat and chin.
Large head clearly distinct from the neck, big golden eyes and vertical pupils.
When threatened it opens its mouth wide and may strike. Mildly venomous but harmless to people.

look.pattern: Plain; pale blue-white throat
look.head: Large broad head; vertical pupils

name: Golden Flying Snake
habitat: Forest, plantations, gardens and village trees; a fast climber in trees and on walls
range: Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, north-east India and the Himalayan foothills (also reported on the islands)
diet: Lizards, geckos, frogs, small birds and bats
ids: A slender, fast tree snake whose scales each have a dark edge, giving a black-and-green, black-and-yellow or black-and-gold net pattern.
Rows of narrow black crossbands cross the body; many have red or orange spots on the neck and flanks and a dark head with pale bars.
Large round eyes and a thin body; it leaps from tree to tree, flattening its body into a concave "wing" so that it glides.
Mildly venomous (rear-fanged) but harmless to people.

look.colour: Yellow-green, gold or green with black edges; red-orange neck spots
look.pattern: Black crossbands and scale edges
look.head: Slim head with big round eyes
look.body: Very slender and slightly ridged along the belly

fact: A flying snake does not truly fly: it launches from a branch, flattens its body into a wide "wing" and glides sideways, steering with S-shaped waves, over 20 m or more.

name: Buff-striped Keelback
habitat: Grassland, paddy fields, gardens, scrub and the edges of ponds and streams; often seen on paths and roads after rain
range: Throughout India from the plains to the lower hills; also Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh and Pakistan
ids: Olive-brown to brown snake with two pale yellowish ("buff") stripes running down the back from the neck, with a series of dark spots or cross-bars between and beside them.
Yellow or white lips and a pair of dark spots (or streaks) on the sides of the head; yellowish belly.
Rough, keeled scales and a fairly short, stout body for its length.
Often basks in grass by day and flees quickly. Harmless; sometimes flattens its neck like a cobra.

look.pattern: Two pale stripes down the back, dark spots between
look.head: Slightly flattened head; yellow lips
look.body: Short and slender with keeled scales

fact: The Buff-striped Keelback is one of the snakes most often seen in India, yet most people do not even recognise it as a snake because it is small and quick.

name: Hill Keelback
habitat: Evergreen forest and shola streams and leaf litter in hill country at middle to high elevations
range: Southern Western Ghats (Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu)
ids: A small, dark brown to olive snake with a black head and a pale yellow or white band (collar) across the neck, with scattered pale flecks along the body.
The bands may be bold in the young and fade in adults. Keeled scales and a rounded head.
A hill-forest snake of the southern Western Ghats; harmless.

look.colour: Dark brown or olive with a black head
look.pattern: Pale yellow collar; faint flecks or bands
look.head: Rounded dark head with a pale collar

name: Beddome's Keelback
habitat: Moist forest floor, stream edges, rocks and plantations in the hills, hunting amphibians in leaf litter
range: Western Ghats of Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra (very similar relatives occur in the northern Western Ghats)
ids: A small brown to greyish-olive keelback that often has a pale (cream or yellowish) band or blotches on the neck, and a dark head with a pale spot on each side.
Pale flecks along the sides give the body a faint banded look; keeled scales and a pale belly.
When disturbed it may flatten the head and neck, and some individuals show an orange collar. Harmless.

look.pattern: Pale neck band and flecks
look.head: Dark head with pale spots

name: Green Keelback
habitat: Grassland, forest edges, farmland and rocky ground; hunts frogs and toads on the ground and in leaf litter
range: Peninsular India: Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Odisha and the Deccan; also Sri Lanka
ids: A stout, olive-green or yellow-green snake with a darker network and a pair of dark chevrons or a black bar behind the head.
A short, broad head that resembles a viper's; when alarmed it flattens its head and neck and strikes in a way that makes people mistake it for a pit viper.
Rough, keeled scales, a short tail and round pupils; the belly is cream or greenish.
Mildly venomous (rear-fanged) and almost never a danger to people.

look.pattern: Dark chevrons or bars behind the head; faint net
look.head: Short broad head with round pupils

fact: Green keelbacks eat toads and store their poison in glands on the neck, which they can present to a predator by arching and flattening the neck.

name: Heller's Red-necked Keelback
habitat: Wet forest edges, streams, paddy fields and gardens in the hills of the north-east; often hunting frogs near water
range: North-east India (Assam, Meghalaya, West Bengal, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh) and eastwards
ids: An olive or brownish snake with a bright orange-red or red patch on the neck and forebody, often with black and yellow markings behind the head.
Keeled scales, round pupils and a slightly widened head. The red neck is the quickest clue.
Rear-fanged: red-necked keelbacks are known to cause serious bleeding after a bite, so they must be treated as dangerous.

look.pattern: Red or orange neck with black and yellow marks
look.head: Slightly widened head; round pupils

name: Andaman Keelback
habitat: Streams, ponds, paddy fields and wet forest on the islands
range: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
ids: A water snake of the islands: brown to olive with dark spots or bars, and dark streaks on the head.
Keeled scales and a rounded head; found beside water. A mild-venom rear-fanged snake, harmless to people.

look.pattern: Dark spots or cross-bars; dark head streaks
look.head: Rounded head with dark streaks

name: Olive Keelback
habitat: Ponds, tanks, canals, paddy fields and streams; swims well and basks on banks
range: Peninsular India (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Odisha and West Bengal); also Sri Lanka
ids: A plain olive, olive-brown or dark grey snake with a bright yellow or cream underside and a yellow stripe at the lower flank where the belly colour meets the back.
No bold pattern. A slim, smooth-looking body with a head only a little wider than the neck.
Strongly aquatic, often seen swimming or resting on banks.

look.colour: Olive, olive-brown or dark grey; yellow belly
look.pattern: Plain; yellow line along the lower flank
look.head: Rounded head, round pupils

name: Large-eyed False Cobra
habitat: Hill and mountain forest, streams and roadsides in the eastern Himalaya and north-east India
range: Sikkim, West Bengal hills, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and neighbouring hills
ids: Spreads a flat, wide "hood" like a cobra when alarmed, and raises the front of its body.
Olive-brown to yellowish with dark bars or a chevron pattern on the neck, a dark arrow mark on the head and a broad dark streak behind the eye.
Round pupils, smooth to weakly keeled scales and large eyes. A mildly venomous but harmless mimic of the cobra.

look.colour: Olive-brown to yellowish with a pale belly
look.pattern: Dark bars on the neck; dark arrow mark and streaks on the head
look.head: Large eyes; head merges into a flattened neck

fact: When threatened it spreads its neck into a hood almost as wide as a small cobra's. It gets away with the bluff because it also hisses and sways.

name: Collared Black-headed Snake
habitat: Hill forest, tea gardens and farmland, in leaf litter, among rocks and in gardens
range: Himalayan foothills and north-east India (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh)
ids: A slender, glossy brown, reddish-brown or olive snake with a black head and a pale (cream or yellow) collar behind it.
Very smooth scales, quick movements and a pale belly.
A harmless skink-hunter of hill country.

look.pattern: Pale collar behind a black head
look.head: Small black head with a pale collar

name: Banded Kukri Snake
habitat: Dry and moist forest, scrub, farmland, gardens and houses; hides under stones and in leaf litter
range: Peninsular India and the Western Ghats; also Sri Lanka
diet: Reptile eggs (especially gecko and skink eggs), skinks and small lizards
ids: A brown, grey-brown or pinkish snake with a series of narrow, pale-edged, dark-brown or reddish cross-bars along the whole body; the bands can be orange-edged.
A small, short head with a dark V- or arrow-shaped mark across the crown; blunt snout and tiny eyes.
Smooth shiny scales; the belly is white or pinkish with dark bars.
Gets its name from the enlarged, curved rear teeth shaped like a kukri knife, which slit open reptile eggs.

look.pattern: Narrow pale-edged cross-bars and a dark V on the head
look.head: Small head with a dark arrow mark

fact: Kukri snakes slice open the shells of gecko and lizard eggs with their enlarged rear teeth and eat the contents.

name: Streaked Kukri Snake
habitat: Dry scrub, rocky country, farmland, forest edges and gardens; shelters under rocks and in termite mounds
range: Most of peninsular India, the Deccan and the Western Ghats, extending into the north-west
diet: Reptile eggs, lizards and small snakes
ids: Pale brown, grey-brown or reddish-brown with thin dark lines (streaks) along the back and flanks, often broken into dashes, plus a dark V mark on the head.
Some individuals have a reddish stripe down the spine or fine dark cross-bars.
A short head, blunt snout and smooth, shiny scales; harmless but may bite readily.

look.pattern: Thin dark streaks and dashes; dark V on the head
look.head: Small head with a dark V mark

name: Tillack's Kukri Snake
habitat: Dry forest, scrub and rocky ground on the Deccan plateau and in western India
range: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa and northern Karnataka
ids: A brown or reddish-brown kukri snake with a series of thin, dark, pale-edged cross-bars or irregular blotches.
A short head with a dark V mark and a pale belly with dark bars.
Very similar to the Banded Kukri Snake; the two are best told apart by locality and scale details.

look.pattern: Thin dark cross-bars or blotches; dark head mark
look.head: Small head with a dark mark

name: Russell's Kukri Snake
habitat: Dry forest, scrub, farmland and the edges of villages in central, eastern and northern India
range: Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Uttarakhand and neighbouring states of eastern and central India
ids: A medium kukri snake in reddish-brown or grey-brown, with a series of dark, pale-edged crossbars and a dark mark on the head.
Short head and blunt snout; smooth shiny scales.
Harmless to people, though bold when handled.

look.pattern: Dark pale-edged crossbars
look.head: Short blunt head with a dark mark

name: Dog-faced Water Snake
habitat: Mangroves, estuaries, tidal creeks, mudflats and brackish backwaters; hides in crab holes
range: Coasts and backwaters of India (Maharashtra, Goa, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal and the Andaman Islands)
ids: A stout, grey-brown to olive snake with dark crossbands or blotches and a pale belly with a stripe along the underside.
Small eyes set high on a slightly flattened head, with upward-pointing nostrils so it can breathe with only its snout out of the water.
Found on mud, in mangroves and brackish water, hence the name; rear-fanged and mildly venomous, harmless to people.

look.pattern: Dark crossbands or blotches
look.head: Small eyes set on top of a flat head; upturned nostrils

fact: The dog-faced water snake lives where the river meets the sea. Its nostrils sit on top of the snout like a hippo's so it can breathe while almost fully under water.

name: Rainbow Water Snake
habitat: Ponds, lakes, marshes, paddy fields and slow rivers, hiding among aquatic plants
range: Eastern and north-eastern India (West Bengal, Odisha, Assam) and across Bangladesh to South-East Asia
ids: A slim, smooth, glossy brown or grey-brown snake that shimmers with an iridescent sheen, with pale stripes along the back or flank and a cream belly.
A narrow, rounded head with small eyes. Lives in water and surfaces to breathe.
Rear-fanged and mildly venomous, harmless to people.

look.colour: Glossy brown with a rainbow sheen
look.pattern: Pale lines along the body
look.head: Narrow rounded head with small eyes

name: Spotted Cat Snake
habitat: Forest, bamboo, plantations, gardens and paddy edges, on the ground and in low vegetation
range: North-east India (Assam, Mizoram, Manipur, Tripura) and eastwards
ids: A slender snake in brown, tan or orange-brown with a row of dark spots or blotches along the back (some individuals are plain orange).
A broad head distinct from a thin neck, large eyes and vertical pupils.
Smooth scales and a long, thin tail; mildly venomous and harmless to people.

look.pattern: A row of dark spots or blotches along the back
look.head: Broad head distinct from the neck; vertical pupils

name: Indo-Chinese Sand Snake
habitat: Open dry forest, scrub, grassland and farmland on sandy or rocky soil
range: Scattered across the north and east of the peninsula (Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Karnataka, Maharashtra) and north-east India
ids: A very slender, fast snake with a pale olive, tan or yellowish-brown body marked by several thin, long, dark and pale stripes.
A narrow head with a dark stripe through the large eye, a long tail and round pupils.
Raises its head high and bobs while it moves quickly over open ground. Mildly venomous (rear-fanged) but harmless to people.

look.pattern: Several thin dark and pale stripes along the body
look.head: Narrow head with a dark eye stripe

name: Olive Forest Snake
habitat: Wet forest floors, stream banks and leaf litter, in hill forest and shola
range: Southern Western Ghats (Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu)
ids: A stout, glossy snake in plain olive, brown or coppery-brown, with a paler yellowish or white belly.
A small, rounded head with a short snout and small eyes; smooth scales.
Often found near forest streams, usually active in wet weather.

look.pattern: Plain, sometimes with faint dark flecks
look.head: Small rounded head

name: Checkered Keelback
habitat: Ponds, paddy fields, streams, drains, wells, lakes and mangroves; close to water almost everywhere
range: Throughout India from the plains to the lower hills, and across the rest of the subcontinent and South-East Asia
active: By day and in the evening
ids: Olive, brown or grey body covered in a dense checkerboard of small dark squares and spots.
Dark streaks on the head: one runs from the eye down to the lip, another back to the corner of the mouth, often with a dark V behind the head.
Rough, keeled scales; rounded snout, round pupils and a head only slightly wider than the neck.
Almost always near water and a quick swimmer, often seen with its head above the surface.
When cornered it flattens its neck and may be mistaken for a cobra, but it is harmless.

look.pattern: Checkerboard of small dark squares; dark streaks on the head
look.head: Oval head, dark streak behind the eye

fact: This is the snake you are most likely to meet beside a pond or paddy field anywhere in India. It is often killed in the belief that it is a cobra or a viper.
